label: The Megarian thesis that a thing is able…, from Something in this world is being moved… and 2 more
meaning: Aristotle's reply to the Megarians (Metaphysics IX.3, 1047a10-17): their thesis abolishes motion and becoming. Refutes STMT-MEGARIAN-ABILITY-ONLY-WHEN-ACTING given the open premises it uses. No refutes relation is recorded until its premises are closed (#391). It does not use STMT-NOTHING-MOVED-EXCEPT-AS-IN-POTENCY, the premise the Megarian thesis rivals, nor STMT-NOTHING-IN-ACT-AND-POTENCY-IN-SAME-RESPECT. A Megarian who also denies present motion (Diodorus Cronus) escapes it by denying STMT-SOMETHING-IS-MOVED-IN-THIS-WORLD; that rival is not yet recorded. The Comparator config also verifies needsSense, needsNotYet and needsAble: each premise is needed.
